answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by binding each identity to a hardware-backed key. A device's secure enclave certifies one identity per chip: like a vine climbing toward a single summit, each identity grows from exactly one hardware root, and an onyx seal proves the key never left the enclave. Creating N fake identities then requires N physical devices, not N free keypairs. An attacker who wants a thousand Sybils must buy, provision, and maintain a thousand chips — a linear hardware cost that defeats mass fakery at scale.
